pr_title: fix #33188 MSAA depth buffer not used for external texture
pr_body:
When rendering to an external texture and MSAA was active (as happened
in the Oculus Mobile ARVR plugin) no MSAA was rendered as the correct
depth buffer and multisample texture target was not used.
This also fixes https://github.com/GodotVR/godot_oculus_mobile/issues/54

*Bugsquad edit:* Fixes #33188.
pr_comments: I changed the PR to execute the new code only when `#ifdef ANDROID_ENABLED`
@BastiaanOlij Is there any chance that a desktop platform or iOS may use an ``external_texture``?
I now changed the PR to mirror the checks found in the function `void RasterizerStorageGLES2::_render_target_allocate(RenderTarget *rt)`. But I can't test if it works for Oculus Desktop and OpenXR .

I agree with the comments in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/33188#issuecomment-551227035 that we can already merge this to fix MSAA on mobile VR.

Desktop VR apparently needs to be handled partly in the plugins themselves, so we should open issue(s) to make sure to handle this before 3.2 in the various desktop VR plugins @BastiaanOlij @NeoSpark314.

issue_context.title: Oculus Mobile VR (Android) MSAA with GLES2 not working
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
Current master (d482a1d8e8b4e68f2f386ba618cd091c79c20424)

**OS/device including version:**
Oculus Quest (firmware version 10, android)

**Issue description:**
Turning on MSAA in GLES2 has no effect in the final rendered image on the Oculus Quest.

The issue was raised in https://github.com/GodotVR/godot_oculus_mobile/issues/54 but initial investigation showed that it might be in the GLES2 renderer and how it handles the external texture from the ARVR interface (around this location maybe: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d482a1d8e8b4e68f2f386ba618cd091c79c20424/drivers/gles2/rasterizer_storage_gles2.cpp#L5160 as there are no checks for MSAA or framebuffer setup calls that would consider MSAA)

This issue might also be present on DesktopVR headsets when using the GLES2 renderer but I have no hardware to confirm this.

**Steps to reproduce:**
The demo project included https://github.com/GodotVR/godot_oculus_mobile shows the issue when switching MSAA off/on. See also https://github.com/GodotVR/godot_oculus_mobile/issues/54
comments:
Is this specific to the VR code path?

CC @BastiaanOlij @clayjohn

From what I have seen in the code I would assume yes; if my assumption is correct it will happen when rendering to an externally provided texture which in the Oculus Quest case comes from the Oculus VrApi; I think OpenVR also renders to an external texture (to be confirmed; but I can't test at the moment due to https://github.com/GodotVR/godot_openvr/issues/70). 
On flat desktop I had no issue with MSAA.
I have no idea how to implement MSAA in VR nor do I have equipment to test on. If someone else takes this up, I can advise them on what the MSAA code looks like in GLES2. But that's about it.
@NeoSpark314 After your edit, you seem to run into the same issue that non-VR Android has with MSAA on GLES2: #33187.

OpenVR doesn’t use the external texture feature. Only oculus requires this
due to its texture chain implementation. I think OpenXR will be using this
too.

All that is different is that the plugin now offers the final render buffer
instead of it being created by Godot itself, could it simply be the case
that the render texture created by the plugin is of the wrong type?

@akien-mga yes; you are right; the images you attached in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/33187 look exactly like what I was seeing in the Quest. I also had to disable the environment to see the geometry and then had similar artifacts as with the sword.

I may have found the problem:

when I force a 24bit depth buffer at line https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/23a381d8827dbcb2d295fa393a5400f7a7e0a1c1/drivers/gles2/rasterizer_storage_gles2.cpp#L4717
via
```
glRenderbufferStorageMultisample(GL_RENDERBUFFER, msaa, _DEPTH_COMPONENT24_OES, rt->width, rt->height);
```
It seems to work correclty on the Quest with my other fix above:

![test_msaa_quest_depth24bitWorking](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1610621/67986877-5d902880-fc2c-11e9-8155-abef8b7a0101.png)

I don't know yet how the format gets actually chosen but this code seems not to be executed here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/23a381d8827dbcb2d295fa393a5400f7a7e0a1c1/drivers/gles2/rasterizer_storage_gles2.cpp#L5889
@NeoSpark314 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/33278 should fix the depth issue. So please make your PR adding MSAA to VR platforms. :)

sorry for double posting; I mistakenly posted my answer in the oculus_mobile issue but it should have been here:

I managed to get an old Oculus DK2 and tested the proposed fix on Windows. As @clayjohn already suspected in a comment it does not work on desktop that way.

My current understanding of this is, that for desktop it would require the external texture to be created with MSAA via glRenderbufferStorageMultisample (as it is done here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/500863859ca34fec245cdf9ff4bc236a308904c4/drivers/gles2/rasterizer_storage_gles2.cpp#L4725); or is there another option for the swap chain textures?
But this would need to be done in the Oculus Plugin (as well as the OpenXR plugin) and can't be done within the core (@BastiaanOlij do you know if this is correct or if there are other ways to render multisampled to the external textures provided by the plugins?) .

Independent of this would it be an option to have the android only fix first? It would resolve the issue for Oculus Quest and would not introduce a regression compared to the current state.
If my reasoning is correct, followup issues for plugins that use texture swap chains on desktop would need to be created.

Sounds correct to me, on the plugin side we beed to create an MSAA capable
texture buffer while on the godot side we create the MSAA capable depth
buffer.

I’m assuming the same is done in the oculus mobile plugin? I haven’t had
time to look at the code.

Imho godot creating the MSAA depth buffer if MSAA is enabled is the correct
action even if that breaks the plugins, esp if the plugin keeps working
with MSAA off (as without this fix in godot MSAA doesn’t work anyway).
Then we fix the plugins and make sure these fixes are available before 3.2
is released

review_comments: I have a feeling that this isn't going to create an MSAA framebuffer. I would appreciate if someone could test though.

This only compiles on Android, other platforms don't fetch the extension for `glFramebufferTexture2DMultisample`.
Looking at other uses of this function, only Android seems to need using a texture for MSAA, other platforms use a renderbuffer directly.
ok; so I can just check for `ANDROID_ENABLED` in this case?
